content: 1. For most non-pregnant adults, it is recommended to set an A1C target of less than 7% to reduce the risk of diabetes-related complications. This target aims to achieve optimal glycemic control while minimizing the risk of hypoglycemia. 2. For non-pregnant adults who are using ambulatory glucose profiles or continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), the goal should be to maintain a time in range (TIR) of greater than 70%, with time spent below range being less than 4%, and time spent below 54 mg/dL being less than 1%. 3. Lower A1C levels may be appropriate if they can be achieved without causing significant episodes of hypoglycemia. 4. In individuals who are at high risk for hypoglycemia or when the burdens of treatment outweigh the benefits, it is advisable to adjust or reduce diabetes medications accordingly. 5. Establishing glycemic goals collaboratively with patients during consultations can enhance their adherence to treatment plans and improve their understanding of diabetes management.
